fields.help:
The note's title. A template whose first line is a # heading names the note instead.
Example: {{leaf}} — {{date:d MMM yyyy}}
fields.title: Title

fields.help:
The Notes folder, levels separated by /. Missing folders are made. Empty: the account's default folder.
Example: Work/Meetings/{{parent}}
fields.title: Folder

fields.help:
A file whose text starts the note. Markdown headings, lists and bold become Notes formatting.
Example: standup.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
The Notes account, by name, if you have more than one. Empty: the default account.
Example: iCloud
fields.title: Account

fields.help:
The note to add to, by its title. It's made the first time if Create if missing is on.
Examples: {{leaf}} · Journal
fields.title: Note

fields.help:
The folder the note is in, levels separated by /.
Example: Projects/{{parent}}
fields.title: Folder

fields.help:
A file whose text is the entry added each time.
Example: worklog.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
What's added to the note, if there's no template. Markdown works; ⌥Return for a new line.
Example: **{{datetime}}** — {{selection}}
fields.title: Entry

fields.help: Make the note if there's none by that name. Off: stop and say so instead.
fields.title: Create if missing

fields.help:
Won't add to a note longer than this many characters: adding rewrites the whole note.
Example: 500000
fields.title: Largest note

fields.help: Won't add to a note with an image in its text, which adding would turn into an attachment.
fields.title: Refuse inline images

fields.help:
The event's title.
Example: {{parent}} with {{leaf}}
fields.title: Title

fields.help:
When it starts: a day, a time, or both. "today" is half an hour from now; other days start at 9:00.
Examples: tomorrow 14:00 · friday · +2h · 2026-10-01 · {{when}}
fields.title: Starts

fields.help:
How long it lasts, in minutes or hours.
Examples: 30m · 1h · 90 min
fields.title: Duration

fields.help:
An alert this many minutes before it starts. Can also be a word in the brackets: [10 min alert].
Example: 10
fields.title: Alert

fields.help:
The calendar, by name. Empty: the one chosen in Settings, else Calendar's default.
Example: Work
fields.title: Calendar

fields.help: The calendar by its identifier, which survives renaming. Usually left empty; name it in Calendar instead.
fields.title: Calendar ID

fields.help:
Notes added to it. Placeholders work.
Example: From {{frontApp}}: {{selection}}
fields.title: Notes

fields.help: Open the new event in Calendar, ready to edit.
fields.title: Open for editing

fields.help:
The reminder.
Example: Call {{leaf}}
fields.title: Title

fields.help:
When it's due, and when it alerts: a length from now, or a day and time.
Examples: +25m · tomorrow 9:00 · friday · {{when}}
fields.title: Due

fields.help:
The Reminders list, by name. Empty: the one chosen in Settings, else the default list.
Example: Errands
fields.title: List

fields.help:
Notes added to it. Placeholders work.
Example: From {{frontApp}}: {{selection}}
fields.title: Notes

fields.help:
The phone number or email address to message. Usually the contact's, which is the default.
Examples: {{contact.phone}} · +44 7700 900123
fields.title: To

fields.help:
The message, ready in Messages — nothing is sent until you press Return there. ⌥Return for a new line.
Example: Running late, there by {{time}}
fields.title: Message

fields.help:
A file whose text is the message instead.
Example: late.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
The address to write to. Usually the contact's, which is the default. Empty: a draft with no one to send to.
Examples: {{contact.email}} · alex@example.com
fields.title: To

fields.help:
The email's subject.
Example: Notes from {{date}}
fields.title: Subject

fields.help:
The email's text, in a draft you send yourself. ⌥Return for a new line.
Example: Hi {{leaf}},
fields.title: Body

fields.help:
A file whose text is the email instead.
Example: weekly-report.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
The number to call. Usually the contact's, which is the default. Only digits, + and dialling marks are used.
Examples: {{contact.phone}} · +44 7700 900123
fields.title: Number

fields.help:
Empty: a phone call through your iPhone. facetime: a FaceTime audio call. macOS asks before dialling.
Example: facetime
fields.title: Via

fields.help:
The app to open. Pick one from the list, type its name, or Choose… it in the Finder.
Example: Visual Studio Code
fields.title: App

fields.help:
The app's identifier, so it's found wherever it's installed. Filled in for you; needed only when the name doesn't find the app.
Example: com.microsoft.VSCode
fields.title: Bundle ID

fields.help:
A file, folder or link for the app to open; ~ for your home folder. Empty: just open the app.
Examples: ~/Projects/{{leaf}} · {{project.path}} · https://github.com
fields.title: Open

fields.help:
A channel or place inside the app, noted until it has a link. Add Open with the link to go there.
Example: general
fields.title: Target

fields.help:
A link to open — web links in your browser, others in their own app — or a file's path. Values placed into a link are encoded; a field that's only a placeholder is the link itself.
Examples: https://duckduckgo.com/?q={{selection}} · {{selection}} · ~/Downloads
fields.title: Link

fields.help:
The text to put on the clipboard, kept exactly. Empty: the node's label. ⌥Return for a new line.
Example: {{contact.phone}}
fields.title: Text

fields.help:
A file whose text is copied instead.
Example: signature.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
auto: formatted too when the text is Markdown — headings, lists, **bold**, *italic*, links — so Mail, Notes and Pages paste it formatted; plain fields get the Markdown. rich: formatted always. plain: the text alone.
Example: plain
fields.title: Format

fields.help:
The text to type at the cursor in the app in front, replacing any selection. Empty: the node's label.
Examples: {{date:d MMMM yyyy}} · "{{selection}}"
fields.title: Text

fields.help:
A file whose text is inserted instead.
Example: signature.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
auto: pasted formatted when the text is Markdown — headings, lists, **bold**, *italic*, links — where the app takes formatting; elsewhere, the Markdown. rich: formatted always. plain: the text alone.
Example: plain
fields.title: Format

fields.help:
The text to put at the cursor in the app in front, replacing any selection — without using the clipboard, so a clipboard manager doesn't record it. Empty: the node's label. ⌥Return for a new line.
Examples: {{date:d MMMM yyyy}} · Kind regards
fields.title: Text

fields.help:
A file whose text is inserted instead.
Example: signature.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
How it goes in. Accessibility: the app replaces its selection with the text, exactly — standard Mac text views take this. Typing: a key press for each character; works nearly everywhere, but new lines press Return, which sends in some chat apps. Inherit: accessibility where the app takes it, else typing.
Example: via: typing
fields.hint: Inherit: accessibility where the app takes it, else typing
fields.title: Via

fields.help:
How long the timer runs, or until when. Empty: a Due value, else the node's label.
Examples: 5 min · 1h 30m · 90s · 16:30 · tomorrow 9:00
fields.title: Length

fields.help:
The shortcut that starts Clock's timers. Empty: KeybowNotes Timer.
Example: My Timer
fields.title: Shortcut

fields.help:
What to search for in Maps. Empty: the node's label.
Examples: coffee · {{selection}} · {{leaf}} near me
fields.title: Search for

fields.help:
A playlist, by name. With no song, album, artist or genre either: the node's label.
Example: Focus
fields.hint: the label, if nothing else is set
fields.title: Playlist

fields.help:
One song in your library, by its title. Wins over everything else; Artist picks between songs that share a title.
Example: So What
fields.title: Song

fields.help:
An album in your library, played in track order. Wins over Playlist, Artist and Genre.
Example: Kind of Blue
fields.title: Album

fields.help:
By itself, plays the artist's songs; with Genre, those in the genre. With a song or an album, picks whose when two share a name. Matches the artist or album artist.
Examples: Miles Davis · {{leaf}}
fields.hint: their songs — or whose album or song
fields.title: Artist

fields.help:
Plays the genre's songs — or, with Artist, that artist's in it.
Example: Jazz
fields.hint: its songs, or an artist's in it
fields.title: Genre

fields.help: Shuffle, or play in order. Inherit leaves Music's setting as it is for a playlist, and shuffles an artist's or a genre's songs, which have no order of their own.
fields.title: Shuffle

fields.help:
The shortcut to run, by its name in the Shortcuts app.
Example: Log Water
fields.title: Shortcut

fields.help:
Text handed to the shortcut as its input.
Examples: {{selection}} · {{clipboard}}
fields.title: Input

fields.help:
What the key does to the stopwatch. Inherit lets the label decide — Start, Stop, Pause, Lap, Split, Reset — and anything else starts or stops it.
Example: do: lap
fields.hint: from the label — Start, Stop, Lap, Reset — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
A file in the templates folder to show, filled in when the key is pressed. Markdown, or an HTML document.
Example: today.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
What to show, when there's no template: Markdown, or an HTML document starting <!DOCTYPE html>.
Example: {{quote file=quotes.md}}
fields.title: Text

fields.help:
Buttons that close it: OK, Cancel, or both. With buttons it stays until one is chosen, and each can run an action of its own. Esc is Cancel.
Example: okCancel
fields.title: Buttons

fields.help:
How long it stays before fading, when it has no buttons. Esc closes it at once.
Example: 15 sec
fields.hint: 15 sec — else long enough to read it
fields.title: Fade after

fields.help:
An action to run when OK is chosen, as though its key were pressed. {{displayed}} is the text shown; Copy and Insert use it when they're given no text.
Example: ok: Copy
fields.title: When OK is chosen

fields.help:
An action to run when Cancel is chosen, or Esc pressed. Usually nothing.
Example: cancel: Notes
fields.title: When Cancel is chosen

fields.help:
A file in the templates folder holding the question, filled in when the key is pressed.
Example: search.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
The question, over the field: Markdown, or an HTML document.
Example: Search Wikipedia for
fields.title: Question

fields.help:
What's in the field to begin with, selected so typing replaces it.
Example: {{selection|}}
fields.title: Starts with

fields.help:
Words shown in the empty field, to say what goes in it.
Example: a word or phrase
fields.title: Hint

fields.help:
A taller field that takes new lines: Return starts one, ⌘Return is OK.
Example: multiline: true
fields.title: Several lines

fields.help:
The action given the answer, as though its key were pressed. {{answer}} is what was typed; Copy and Insert use it when they're given no text.
Example: ok: Insert
fields.title: When OK is chosen

fields.help:
An action to run when Cancel is chosen, or Esc pressed. Usually nothing.
Example: cancel: Display
fields.title: When Cancel is chosen

fields.help:
Where on the screen: full, a half — left, right, top, bottom — or a quarter — topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft, bottomRight. Halves fill the height or the width. All within the screen less the menu bar and an always-shown Dock. Left out, a label like “Top left” says.
Example: topLeft
fields.hint: else the label — else where it is now
fields.title: Place

fields.help:
Which screen to put it on: next or previous, main (the one with the menu bar), a number counting from the left, or part of a display's name. With no place, the window keeps its share of the screen.
Example: next
fields.hint: next, previous, main, 2, or a name — else its own
fields.title: Screen

fields.help:
What to show: all — Mission Control, every window — app, the windows of the app in front, or desktop. Left out, a label like “App windows” or “Desktop” says. Pressing the key again puts things back.
Example: app
fields.title: Show

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 1, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 1

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 2, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 2

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 3, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 3

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 4, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 4

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 5, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 5

fields.help:
The desktop to show on screen 6, counting screens from the left, and that screen's desktops from 1, left to right as Mission Control shows them. no change leaves it as it is, even when a branch above sets it. Left out, the branch above decides — else it's left as it is.
Example: 2
fields.title: Screen 6

fields.help:
What to control, by its entity ID — or several, separated by commas. The list is what Home Assistant has.
Example: light.desk_lamp
fields.title: Entity

fields.help:
What to do, as Home Assistant names it: turn_on, turn_off, toggle, or a whole name like climate.set_hvac_mode. Left out: a toggle; on, for a light given a brightness or colour; the temperature, for a thermostat given one; on, for a scene or script.
Example: turn_off
fields.title: Service

fields.help:
A light's brightness, 0 to 100.
Example: 40
fields.title: Brightness

fields.help:
A light's colour: #rrggbb, or a name Home Assistant knows.
Example: orange
fields.title: Colour

fields.help:
A white light's warmth, in kelvin: 2700 is warm, 6500 daylight.
Example: 2700
fields.title: Colour temperature

fields.help:
What a thermostat is set to, in Home Assistant's units.
Example: 21
fields.title: Temperature

fields.help:
A thermostat's mode, as Home Assistant names it.
Example: heat
fields.title: Mode

fields.help:
For a number, a select or a text entity: the value to set — or the option to choose.
Example: 3
fields.title: Value

fields.help:
Anything else the service takes, as name: value pairs separated by commas — or as JSON.
Example: transition: 2
fields.title: More

fields.help:
now — the meeting under way, or the next today; in a meeting's last five minutes, the next if it starts within ten. next — the next meeting to start, whatever's under way.
Example: next
fields.hint: now: the one under way, else the next today
fields.title: Which meeting

fields.help:
now — the meeting under way, or the next today; in a meeting's last five minutes, the next if it starts within ten. next — the next meeting to start, whatever's under way.
Example: next
fields.hint: now: the one under way, else the next today
fields.title: Which meeting

fields.help:
A file in the templates folder to add, filled in when the key is pressed.
Example: decision.md
fields.title: Template

fields.help:
What to add to the meeting's notes, as its own paragraph.
Example: {{time}} — {{selection}}
fields.title: Text

fields.help:
Words from the title of the reminder to tick off. Left out, it's the one due next, or overdue — {{reminder}}.
Example: Call the bank
fields.title: Reminder

fields.help:
The Reminders list to look in. Left out, the lists chosen in Settings, else all.
Example: Errands
fields.title: List

fields.help:
What the key does: up, down, mute, unmute, or toggle — mute, or unmute if it's muted. Left out, the label says: Up, Louder, Down, Quieter, Mute (which toggles, as the key on the keyboard does), Unmute, or a level like 40%.
Example: up
fields.hint: else the label — Louder, Quieter, Mute — else toggle mute
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Sets the volume to this, in percent, and unmutes.
Example: 30
fields.title: Level

fields.help:
How far up or down one press goes, in percent. Left out, a sixteenth, as the volume keys go.
Example: 10
fields.title: Step

fields.help:
What the key does to the microphone: toggle, mute or unmute. Left out, a label saying Unmute unmutes, and anything else — Mute included — toggles.
Example: mute
fields.hint: else the label — Unmute — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Brighter or dimmer: up or down. Left out, the label says — Brighter, Up, Dimmer, Darker, Down, or a level like 40%.
Example: up
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Sets the brightness to this, in percent.
Example: 30
fields.title: Level

fields.help:
How far one press goes, in percent. Left out, a sixteenth, as the brightness keys go.
Example: 10
fields.title: Step

fields.help:
Which screen: all of them, built-in, main (the one with the menu bar), a number counting from the left, or part of a screen's name. Left out, the one the pointer is on. Apple's screens are set as the brightness keys set them; others over their cable (DDC/CI), on an Intel Mac, when the monitor allows it.
Example: all
fields.hint: all, built-in, main, 2, or a name — else the pointer's
fields.title: Screen

fields.help:
Turns Wi‑Fi on or off, or toggles it. Left out, a label saying On or Off decides, and anything else toggles. 
Example: off
fields.hint: else the label — On, Off — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Turns Bluetooth on or off, or toggles it. Left out, a label saying On or Off decides, and anything else toggles. Off disconnects Bluetooth keyboards, mice and headphones until it's back on: the keypad, on USB, can turn it on again.
Example: off
fields.hint: else the label — On, Off — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Turns Night Shift on or off, or toggles it, until its schedule next changes it. Left out, a label saying On or Off decides, and anything else toggles.
Example: on
fields.hint: else the label — On, Off — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Dark, light, or the other one. Left out, a label saying just Dark or Light decides, and anything else toggles. macOS asks once whether KeybowNotes may control System Events, which makes the change.
Example: dark
fields.hint: else the label — Dark, Light — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
Keeps the Mac and its screens from sleeping, lets them sleep again, or toggles. Left out, a label saying On or Off decides, and anything else toggles.
Example: on
fields.hint: else the label — On, Off — else toggle
fields.title: Do

fields.help:
How long to stay awake, or until when. Left out, a label like “1 hour” says, else until it's turned off. Pressing it again while it's on, with a duration, starts the time again.
Examples: 45m · 2h · 17:30
fields.title: For

fields.help:
Which Focus: Sleep unless this says another, by its name in System Settings → Focus.
Example: Do Not Disturb
fields.title: Focus

fields.help:
The shortcut that switches it, made once in the Shortcuts app. Left out, “KeybowNotes <Focus> Focus”: Get Current Focus; If it's the Focus, Set Focus to turn it off; Otherwise, Set Focus to turn it on until turned off.
Example: Toggle Sleep
fields.title: Shortcut

values.help: The label of the key pressed: the last in the path.
values.name: leaf
values.title: The key's label

values.help: The label pressed before it. A key on the tree's first row is its own parent.
values.name: parent
values.title: The label above it

values.help: Every label pressed, separated by “ / ”.
values.name: path
values.title: The whole path

values.help: The labels separated by /, for a Notes folder or a file's path. A / inside a label becomes -.
values.name: folderPath
values.title: The path as folders

values.help: The path as folders, without the key's own label.
values.name: parentPath
values.title: The folders above it

values.help: The label pressed first, on the tree's first row.
values.name: level1
values.title: The first label

values.help: The second label pressed. Empty when the path is shorter.
values.name: level2
values.title: The second label

values.help: The third label pressed. Empty when the path is shorter.
values.name: level3
values.title: The third label

values.help: The fourth label pressed. Empty when the path is shorter.
values.name: level4
values.title: The fourth label

values.help: The tree the key is in: main, row2, row3 or bottom.
values.name: tree
values.title: Which tree

values.help: The person this key is about: the deepest label on the path that's in # contacts, or the one a contact: value names. Empty when there's none.
values.name: contact.name
values.title: The contact's name

values.help: From their entry in # contacts.
values.name: contact.phone
values.title: Their phone number

values.help: From their entry in # contacts.
values.name: contact.email
values.title: Their email address

values.help: Anything else their entry in # contacts holds, by its name.
values.name: contact.<field>
values.title: Another of their fields

values.help: The project this key is about: the deepest label on the path that's in # projects, or the one a project: value names. Empty when there's none.
values.name: project.name
values.title: The project's name

values.help: From its entry in # projects.
values.name: project.path
values.title: Its folder

values.help: Anything else its entry in # projects holds, by its name.
values.name: project.<field>
values.title: Another of its fields

values.help: When the key is pressed. A format after a colon changes how it's written, in Unicode's date patterns.
values.name: date
values.title: The date

values.help: When the key is pressed. A format after a colon changes how it's written, in Unicode's date patterns.
values.name: time
values.title: The time

values.help: When the key is pressed. A format after a colon changes how it's written, in Unicode's date patterns.
values.name: datetime
values.title: The date and time

values.help: When the key is pressed. A format after a colon changes how it's written, in Unicode's date patterns.
values.name: weekday
values.title: The day of the week

values.help: The ISO week number when the key is pressed, 1 to 53.
values.name: isoWeek
values.title: The week of the year

values.help: The text selected in the app in front when the key is pressed, trimmed. Read only when an action uses it. With nothing selected it's missing, which stops most actions: {{selection|}} makes empty fine.
values.name: selection
values.title: The selected text

values.help: What's on the clipboard when the key is pressed: its text, trimmed — or an image or a PDF, which a {{#ai}} block sends as itself, and anything else describes.
values.name: clipboard
values.title: The clipboard

values.help: The app in front when the key is pressed.
values.name: frontApp
values.title: The app in front

attributes.help: A file to go through instead of a value: in the templates folder, or a full or ~/ path.
attributes.name: file

attributes.help: Only the rows that pass: a column, then = != < <= > >= ~ (contains) or !~, then a value; tests joined with “and”. A column alone means it has something in it.
attributes.name: where

attributes.help: Columns to order the rows by, each asc or desc: numbers as numbers.
attributes.name: sort

attributes.help: At most this many rows: after where and sort.
attributes.name: limit

attributes.help: Put between the rows: \n for a new line.
attributes.name: separator

attributes.help: Names for the columns, when the data has no header row; none to number them only.
attributes.name: columns

attributes.help: How to read it, when guessing gets it wrong.
attributes.name: format

values.help: Its contents once for each row of a value — {{#each clipboard}}, {{#each api.github}} — or of a file: {{#each file='team.csv'}}. Rows are read from CSV, cells copied from a spreadsheet, JSON, a Markdown table, or a line each; the first row of CSV names the columns. Inside, {{Name}} is the row's Name column, and {{1}} its first.
values.name: each
values.title: Each row

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: written once before the rows, when there are any.
values.name: header
values.title: Before the rows

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: written once after the rows, when there are any.
values.name: footer
values.title: After the rows

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: written in place of the rows when there are none.
values.name: empty
values.title: When there are none

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: 1 for the first row shown, then 2, 3…
values.name: @number
values.title: The row's number

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: how many rows are shown, after where and limit.
values.name: @count
values.title: How many rows

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: the row's cells, separated by tabs — for a list of single items, the item.
values.name: @row
values.title: The whole row

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: the columns' names, separated by tabs.
values.name: @columns
values.title: The columns' names

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: the numbers in a column added up, over the rows shown.
values.name: @sum.<column>
values.title: A column's total

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: the average of the numbers in a column.
values.name: @average.<column>
values.title: A column's average

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: a column's smallest value: a number, a date, a word.
values.name: @min.<column>
values.title: A column's least

values.help: Inside {{#each}}: a column's largest value: a number, a date, a word.
values.name: @max.<column>
values.title: A column's most

values.help: The stopwatch's time, running or stopped.
values.name: stopwatch
values.title: Its time

values.help: The stopwatch's time, in whole seconds.
values.name: stopwatch.seconds
values.title: Its time in seconds

values.help: How long each lap took, in order. Empty before the first lap.
values.name: stopwatch.laps
values.title: Each lap's length

values.help: The time since the start at each lap, in order.
values.name: stopwatch.splits
values.title: The time at each lap

attributes.help: The model to ask, else the one in Settings → Claude.
attributes.name: model

attributes.help: How hard it thinks before replying, else as Settings → Claude says.
attributes.name: effort

attributes.help: Who's asked: Claude, the only one so far.
